summary: Implement a fixed-capacity circular queue (ring buffer) with O(1) operations.
mainInsight: Use a fixed array with head and tail indices that wrap modulo capacity; track the size (or leave one slot empty) so full and empty states are distinguishable.

approaches.name: Array with head/tail/size
approaches.summary: Write at tail, read at head, wrap with % cap; size disambiguates full vs empty.

approaches.name: Array with a wasted slot
approaches.summary: Capacity k+1; full when (tail+1) % cap == head.

approaches.name: Linked list
approaches.summary: Nodes with head/tail pointers and a count.

promptVariants: What technique makes the array queue reuse freed slots?
How do head and tail move in a circular queue?
options: Shift all remaining elements left on every dequeue operation
Reallocate a bigger array whenever the tail reaches the end
Sort the array after each enqueue so free slots come first
cards.explanation: Wrapping with % cap lets head/tail cycle without moving elements.

promptVariants: Why do you need either a size counter or a wasted slot?
How do you tell a full queue from an empty one when head == tail?
cards.answer: When head == tail the queue could be completely empty or completely full. Tracking size (or reserving one empty slot) removes the ambiguity: empty = size 0, full = size == capacity.
cards.explanation: Your size field makes isEmpty/isFull trivial.

promptVariants: Complete the statement: Time of every operation: ___
Space used by the ring buffer of capacity k: ___
Complete the statement: Space used by the ring buffer of capacity k: ___
cards.explanation: A fixed array of k slots.

promptVariants: Why does Rear() use `self.queue[self.tail - 1]` and what happens when tail == 0?
Rewrite Rear() without relying on negative indexing.
cards.answer: tail points to the NEXT write position, so the last element is at tail - 1. When tail == 0 (after wrapping) tail - 1 is -1, which Python resolves to the last array slot - correct but implicit. An explicit version is `self.queue[(self.tail - 1) % self.cap]`.
keyPoints: -1 index wraps in Python; use % cap in other languages
cards.explanation: Alternatively store head and size and compute (head + size - 1) % cap.

promptVariants: After enQueue to a full queue what happens?
What do enQueue/deQueue return on full/empty?
options: enQueue returns False and changes nothing; so does deQueue on empty
It overwrites the oldest element and returns True for the new value
It raises an exception that the calling code must then handle
It grows the buffer and then stores the new value as usual
cards.answer: enQueue returns False and changes nothing; so does deQueue on empty
cards.explanation: The API reports failure via booleans and leaves the queue unchanged.

incorrectOptionExplanations.It overwrites the oldest element and ret: That would be a different (overwriting) ring buffer.
